advances: The lower-endpoint argument of accepted fact `5b41a693b247f547` extends to a boundary-complete three-polynomial \(A_0\) triangle-cap family.  The family includes the opposite endpoint order, the tied order, both zero-offset strata, and the two nontrivial cyclic positive-quadrant cells, without any division.  It excludes the strict point of accepted fact `6090beea12ef2770`, but it does not empty the full inherited opposite system: a new strict rational survivor is given and checked below.  Thus this mechanism alone does not close the opposite branch or prove the locked \(2/9\) target; a further simultaneous polygon-completion condition is still necessary.
author: mp_r107_opposite_a0_triangle_cap
proof:
We first prove a boundary-complete quadrant lemma.  Let \(C\) be a compact convex polygon in affine coordinates \((T,R)\), with coordinate area equal to \(\Delta\) times physical area.  Suppose
\[
C\cap\{R=0\}=[q_-,q]\times\{0\},
\qquad q\ge0,
\]
and \((p,-r)\in C\), where \(r\ge0\).  Let \(E\) be the part of \(C\) in \(T,R\ge0\), and let its physical area be \(D\).

Assume first \(r>0\).  For \((T,R)\in E\) with \(R>0\), the segment from \((p,-r)\) to \((T,R)\) meets \(R=0\) at
\[
\left(\frac{rT+Rp}{r+R},0\right).
\]
This point belongs to the full section, so
\[
rT+(p-q)R\le rq.
\tag{1}
\]
The same inequality holds when \(R=0\), because then \(T\le q\).  If \(p>q\), (1) contains \(E\) in the triangle
\[
T\ge0,\qquad R\ge0,\qquad
rT+(p-q)R\le rq,
\]
whose coordinate area is
\[
\frac{rq^2}{2(p-q)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
2\Delta D(p-q)\le rq^2.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(p=q\), (1) is the strip \(T\le q\), and (2) is automatic.  If \(p<q\), the left side of (2) is nonpositive, so (2) is again automatic.  Finally, if \(r=0\) and \(p>q\), the point \((p,0)\) contradicts the fact that \(q\) is the right endpoint of the full section.  If \(r=0\) and \(p\le q\), (2) is automatic.  Thus (2) is valid in every order and on every zero or tangent stratum, without dividing by \(r\), \(q\), or \(p-q\).

Apply the lemma first in the original coordinates \((T,R)=(X,Y)\).  Up to null cutting lines, the positive quadrant has physical area \(b\).  Its full \(R=0\) section has right endpoint
\[
q=\beta+H=\delta-\tau,
\]
and the lower diagonal endpoint gives
\[
(p,-r)=(\delta+\gamma,-\gamma).
\]
Hence \(p-q=\gamma+\tau\), and (2) is exactly (Tb).

For any other diagonal point \(t\in[\gamma,\gamma+K]\), the same argument gives
\[
2\Delta b(t+\tau)\le t(\delta-\tau)^2.
\tag{3}
\]
When \(\tau\ge0\), the active upper bound \(t/(t+\tau)\) is nondecreasing in \(t\): for \(t\ge\gamma\),
\[
\gamma(t+\tau)\le t(\gamma+\tau).
\]
Thus the lower endpoint \(t=\gamma\) is strongest whenever \(\gamma+\tau>0\).  If \(\gamma=\tau=0\), choose any \(t\in(0,K]\) in (3), cancel the positive \(t\), and obtain (T0).  Independently, (T0) is also the direct containment of \(P_0\) in
\[
\{X\ge0,\ Y\ge0,\ X+Y\le\delta\}.
\]

For \(P_\ell\), use
\[
(T,R)=(p_k,-p_\ell)=(\delta-X-Y,-Y).
\]
This affine change has determinant magnitude one, and its positive quadrant has physical area \(c\) up to null unsupported cells.  The full \(R=0\) section has
\[
T\in[\tau,\delta-\beta],
\]
so its right endpoint is \(q=\delta-\beta\).  The lower \(X=0\) endpoint becomes
\[
(p,-r)=(\delta-\alpha,-\alpha).
\]
Thus \(p-q=\beta-\alpha\), and (2) is (Tc).

More generally, a point \((0,s)\) of the vertical chord gives
\[
2\Delta c(\beta-s)\le s(\delta-\beta)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
If \(s<\beta\), the corresponding active cap factor \(s/(\beta-s)\) is nondecreasing in \(s\); for \(\alpha\le s<\beta\),
\[
\frac{\alpha}{\beta-\alpha}
\le\frac{s}{\beta-s}
\]
by cross multiplication.  Hence \(s=\alpha\) is strongest.  If \(\alpha\ge\beta\), no point of the vertical chord has \(s<\beta\), and (Tc) is automatic.  This proves every ordering and tie asserted above.

The cyclic positive-quadrant targets are \(P_0\) in \((p_j,p_\ell)\), \(P_\ell\) in \((p_k,-p_\ell)\), and \(P_0\cup P_\ell\) in \((p_j,p_k)\).  The first two are the applications just proved.  In the third coordinates, the remaining chord \(p_\ell=0\) is
\[
(p_j,p_k)=(X,\delta-X),
\qquad X\in[\beta,\beta+H],
\]
and lies inside the nonnegative quadrant.  It cannot play the role of \((p,-r)\) with \(r>0\).  Reversing the two axes does not change this.  The two exterior supported cells likewise give only unbounded wedges under the corresponding endpoint half-planes.  Therefore (T0), (Tb), and (Tc) are the complete cyclic family produced by this triangle-cap mechanism.

\]
\[

\]
The total areas and common crossing are
\[
M=\frac{1436009}{20000},\qquad
m=\frac{21}{2},\qquad

t=\frac{206001}{10000}.
\]
In particular,
\[
M-t=\frac{1024007}{20000}>0,\qquad
M-m=\frac{1226009}{20000}>0.
\]
The three cap triples, their sums, left-tail slacks, and proper-cap slacks are

\begin{array}{c|ccc|c|c|ccc}
i&u_i&v_i&C_i&u_i+v_i+C_i&C_i+m-t&M-u_i&m-v_i&\kappa-C_i\\ \hline

\]
so every crossing, proper-cap, tail, finite-interior, \(M\ge m\), \(0<t<M\), and \(W=0\) condition in the inherited system is strict where it is not an identity.

For the sharp trace lower bounds, let
\[
\eta_j=\sqrt{a(a+b)}-a,\qquad
\eta_k=\sqrt{d(d+b)}-d,
\]
\[
\eta_\ell=\sqrt{(c+d)(b+c+d)}-(c+d).
\]
Here
\[
a(a+b)=d(d+b)=\frac{1430007}{200000000}<1,
\]
so \(\eta_j,\eta_k<1\).  Also
\[
(c+d+5)^2-(c+d)(b+c+d)
=\frac{261750999}{40000000}>0,
\]
so \(\eta_\ell<5\).  Since \(2\Delta/\delta=1/50\), the three \(A_0\) traces \(J=K=H=1/10\) strictly exceed their lower bounds.  Every \(A_2\)-to-\(A_0\) trace gap equals \(1/100\), so every strict trace disjunction is selected by a nonzero gap.  The \(A_2\) product slack is
\[
2\Delta g_0-J_2H_2=\frac{2879}{10000}>0.
\]
Moreover \(3-2\sqrt2>1/6\), for example because \((17/12)^2>2\), and hence
\[
KH=\frac1{100}
<\frac1{10}
<\frac35(3-2\sqrt2)
=2\Delta c(3-2\sqrt2).
\]
The same estimates give
\[
2\Delta\eta_k\eta_\ell<10
<1500=g_0\delta^2,
\]
\[
2\Delta\eta_k\eta_\ell<10
<500<c(3-2\sqrt2)\delta^2.
\]
Thus all trace and common-plane inequalities from accepted fact `2b42506f5de09be1` hold strictly.

The old strict rational point of `6090beea12ef2770` violates (Tc), exactly as certified in accepted fact `5b41a693b247f547`.  The new survivor shows that this exclusion is local to that endpoint placement and cannot by itself complete the opposite branch.
statement:
Use the \(A_0\) coordinate and exact-cell convention of accepted facts `989c9b585d2b42cc` and `fa0e57b225178b3b`.  Thus coordinate area is \(\Delta>0\) times physical area,
\[
p_j=X,\qquad p_\ell=Y,\qquad p_k=\delta-X-Y,\qquad \delta>0,
\]
the only positive-area cells are \(P_j,P_0,P_\ell,P_{k\ell}\), with respective physical areas \(a,b,c,d>0\), and the full cutting-line chords are
\[
X=0,\quad Y\in[\alpha,\alpha+J],
\]
\[
Y=0,\quad X\in[\beta,\beta+H],
\]
\[
X+Y=\delta,\quad (X,Y)=(\delta+t,-t),
\quad t\in[\gamma,\gamma+K],
\]
where
\[
J,H,K>0,\qquad
0\le\alpha\le\alpha+J\le\delta,
\]
\[
0\le\beta\le\beta+H\le\delta,\qquad
\gamma\ge0,\qquad
\tau=\delta-\beta-H\ge0.
\]
Every such polygon satisfies the following finite polynomial family:
\[
\mathcal T_0:\qquad 2\Delta b\le\delta^2,
\tag{T0}
\]
\[
\mathcal T_b:\qquad
2\Delta b(\gamma+\tau)
\le\gamma(\delta-\tau)^2,
\tag{Tb}
\]
\[
\mathcal T_c:\qquad
2\Delta c(\beta-\alpha)
\le\alpha(\delta-\beta)^2.
\tag{Tc}
\]
These statements are literal on every boundary.  In particular:

1. If \(\beta>\alpha>0\), (Tc) is the active lower-endpoint triangle cap.  If \(\beta=\alpha\), the containing half-plane is a strip and (Tc) is automatic.  If \(\beta<\alpha\), its left side is negative and it is again automatic.  If \(\alpha=0<\beta\), (Tc) excludes the stratum because \(c>0\).

2. If \(\gamma+\tau>0\), (Tb) is the active cyclic \(P_0\)-cap.  If \(\gamma=\tau=0\), (Tb) is \(0\le0\), and the limiting nonzero endpoint of the diagonal chord gives (T0).  If \(\gamma=0<\tau\), (Tb) excludes the stratum because \(b>0\).

3. These are all single-external-chord triangle caps for the three cyclic positive-quadrant \(A_0\) cells or unions.  The third cyclic pair has target \(P_0\cup P_\ell\), while its remaining \(Y=0\) chord lies inside that positive quadrant, so it supplies no external point and no additional triangle-cap row.

Let \(\mathcal S_\triangle\) be the full opposite necessary system asserted in accepted fact `6090beea12ef2770`, which includes the common-plane conditions of accepted fact `2b42506f5de09be1` and the full-section and endpoint systems of `989c9b585d2b42cc` and `fa0e57b225178b3b`, augmented by (T0), (Tb), and (Tc).  Then
\[
\mathcal S_\triangle\ne\varnothing.
\]
